title: Fix off-by-one in seq-length bucket boundary logic (scheduler -> selector context)
author: Lena Fischer
release_notes: Fixes seq-length bucket classification at exact boundary values (e.g., 512/1024/2048 tokens) to ensure stable kernel selection + telemetry bucketing for selector v2.
description: Context: During the benchmark sweep for kernel selector v2 we saw discontinuities in p95 for long-context runs where prompts were generated at exact bucket boundaries (e.g., 2048) and occasionally landed in the next bucket. This was traced to an off-by-one / inclusive-exclusive mismatch between how scheduler computed effective sequence length and how we mapped it into selector "seq_bucket" (prefill regime). Impact: Wrong bucket => wrong kernel family choice in the table for some GPUs (notably A10/L4), plus noisy telemetry where boundary-length prompts appeared split across buckets. This PR fixes bucket boundary handling to be deterministic and consistent with the documented bucket definitions. Change summary: - Make bucket definitions explicit as half-open intervals [lower, upper) with a single canonical helper used by scheduler->runtime context construction. - Align "effective_prompt_tokens" (prefill) bucketing with telemetry labels (same function, same constants). - Add targeted unit tests for boundary values (exactly at lower/upper edges) and randomized property-style checks to prevent regressions when bucket sets change. - Add a trace annotation in debug builds (guarded) to print the computed boundaries for quick validation in local repro. Root cause: We previously treated upper bounds as inclusive in one call site (<=) while the table/bucket documentation assumed exclusive (<). At exact edges we would incorrectly advance to the next bucket. Notes: This only changes the bucketing signal and does not change the selector v2 table itself; it does change which row is selected at exact boundary values. That is intended and matches the benchmark plan buckets. Testing: - Added unit tests in scheduling module for: 0, 1, 511, 512, 513, 1023, 1024, 1025, 2047, 2048, 2049 tokens. - Ran benchmark-lab smoke locally (subset) and confirmed boundary prompts now hit the expected rows and reduce variance. - CI includes runtime_unit + runtime_integration + selector_conformance_smoke. Commits (squash): 1) scheduler: define canonical seq bucket helper + constants 2) runtime: use canonical helper when building selector context 3) tests: add boundary + randomized checks 4) debug: add optional trace annotation for computed bucket bounds Files/areas changed (high level): - runtime/scheduler/seq_bucket.cc, runtime/scheduler/seq_bucket.h - runtime/scheduler/request_context.cc - runtime/selector/context_builder.cc - runtime/selector/tests/seq_bucket_test.cc - runtime/trace/annotations.cc Review notes: - Please sanity check the interval semantics vs the bucket docs in the design doc and benchmark harness. - Marcus/Rina: tests are written to fail loudly if buckets change; if you prefer less coupling, we can relax the randomized test to only check monotonicity + determinism. Review conversation: Grace Kim: "Thanks for chasing this down. Can you confirm we’re not changing decode bucketing?" Lena Fischer (author): "Correct—this only affects prefill effective prompt tokens bucketing. Decode path uses token position buckets derived from a different signal and is unchanged in this PR." Omar El-Sayed: "Can you ensure the helper is used in telemetry too? Otherwise we’ll still see split labels." Lena Fischer: "Yep—telemetry label generation now calls the same helper; removed the local <= logic." Marcus Reed: "Can we add a regression test for exact 2048 since that was the spike in the sweep?" Lena Fischer: "Added explicit 2048 case + assertion of bucket id." Rina Kobayashi: "Bench harness uses [lower, upper) in Python; this matches. Approved." CI: - buildkite/runtime-unit: PASS - buildkite/runtime-integration: PASS - buildkite/selector-conformance-smoke: PASS - lint: PASS Merge: Squash merged to main. Follow-ups: None required for functionality; benchmark sweep will be re-run as part of ENG-3929 with this fix included.
